title: Feature Request: Support multiple account login and switching (like `gh auth switch`)
body:
## Feature Request: Multiple Account Support / Account Switching

### Problem
Users who work across multiple contexts (e.g., personal, Company A, Company B)
with separate Claude.ai accounts cannot quickly switch between them. There is
no way to see which account is currently active at a glance, and no fast
switching mechanism exists.

This creates real risks:
- Accidentally using a personal account for confidential company work
- Using a company account for personal projects (policy violation)
- No visual indicator of the currently active account in the workflow

Currently, switching requires a full logout → login cycle with browser
authentication every time, making it impractical to switch frequently.

### Expected Behavior
Similar to `gh auth switch` in GitHub CLI:
- Store credentials for multiple accounts locally
- Switch accounts with a single command: `claude auth switch`
- Show the currently active account clearly (e.g., `claude auth status`)

### Example Workflow
```bash
$ claude auth switch
? Select account:
  > personal@gmail.com (Personal - Pro)
    alice@company-a.com (Company A - Teams)
    alice@company-b.com (Company B - Teams)
```

### Current Workaround
```bash
claude auth logout && claude auth login --email other@example.com
```
This triggers a full browser authentication flow every time.

### Use Case
Freelancers, contractors, and consultants working across multiple
organizations need reliable, frictionless account switching to avoid
accidental cross-account usage.
author: aice-kazuki-okura

top_comments.body:
**Feature proposal: `/account` command for multi-account management**

Building on the idea of named profiles, I'd like to propose a `/account` command (or `claude account`) that makes multi-account management a first-class experience:
```
$ claude account

Logged-in accounts:
  * work     →  john@company.com    [default for new instances]
    personal →  john@gmail.com

Switch account for this session:
  > work (current)
    personal
    + Add another account
```

top_comments.body:
In the meantime while this isn't built in, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` gets you most of the way there. Each config directory gets its own Keychain entry so auth is fully isolated — you can have work and personal running side by side in different terminals without them touching each other.

top_comments.author: zeroarst
top_comments.body:
On Linux/WSL2 there's no Keychain, so `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` doesn't isolate credentials — the second profile always falls
 through to `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. We've confirmed the credentials file exists at
`~/.claude-personal/.credentials.json` but Claude Code doesn't pick it up.

Currently using a symlink swap approach (swapping `~/.claude.json` and `~/.claude/.credentials.json` before launch)
but it's not parallel-safe. Would love to know if claude-profile handles this on Linux.
